title: Check every security layer before enabling Lava or API behavior
distilled_summary: For Lava, Helix, and REST-backed work, agents should verify page or block access, enabled Lava commands, entity authorization, controller permissions, REST key identity, CSRF posture, and CORS scope separately. A visible page or working endpoint is not enough evidence that the full operation is appropriately constrained.

title: Use SQL and Dynamic Data only with explicit safety boundaries
distilled_summary: When SQL is the clearest Rock reporting surface, agents should parameterize user input, bound result sets, avoid broad column selection, document unusual filters and date windows, and confirm whether the report exposes sensitive person, giving, child, prayer, or counseling data. Dynamic Data-style blocks are best treated as read-only reporting surfaces, with writes handled through reviewed workflow, API, or entity-command paths.

title: Preflight check-in and registration changes before launch
distilled_summary: For check-in labels, event registration check-in, or QR-driven mobile flows, agents should identify the event or area scope, confirm launch windows and role gates, verify that already-checked-in records are filtered correctly, run maintenance scripts in dry-run mode first, and validate live behavior with representative child, parent, team member, and registrant cases before go-live.
